title: Documenting Managerial Overrides in AI Supported Pharmaceutical Field Decisions: A Proposed Record Structure and Testable Governance Hypotheses
content: Human oversight is often described as a manager's ability to reject an AI recommendation, but a count of accepted and rejected recommendations reveals little about decision quality. This conceptual paper asks what information a pharmaceutical commercial organization would need to distinguish a justified override from unsupported disagreement, a data correction or an unauthorized exception. A targeted synthesis of human–automation interaction, algorithm reliance and model-documentation research informs a proposed decision record linking the recommendation, the evidence available at the time, the manager's stated reason, the action and a later review. Four hypotheses specify how record completeness, outcome separation, proportionate documentation and independent review could affect auditability and learning. A hypothetical territory-planning example and a prospective evaluation design illustrate the proposal. No employee data, interviews or organizational outcomes are reported; the record structure and hypotheses require empirical testing.
